plan_a_advantages: More varied training stimuli (long runs, tempo, hills, cross-training) directly addressing trail running demands.
Includes dedicated long runs, which are essential for building the aerobic base needed for longer trail races.
plan_b_advantages: More concise and efficient in terms of total training time.
Strong emphasis on threshold training, which can be beneficial for improving running economy and speed once a solid aerobic base is established.
reasoning: Plan A is better suited for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates a broader range of training stimuli crucial for trail running performance. It includes dedicated long runs, tempo runs, and hill intervals – all vital for building both aerobic endurance and the specific strength required for navigating varied terrain. Plan B, while well-structured, focuses heavily on threshold work and shorter, more consistent efforts, potentially neglecting the crucial development of sustained power and the ability to handle longer, undulating trails.  The inclusion of cross-training also provides a valuable recovery and supplemental fitness component.
